documents.title: Morse–Hedlund: p(L) = L + 1 for all L iff Sturmian
documents.source_line: ** [`research-journal.md`](../research-journal.md) — Round 7, line 566; "The ten things that stand" §10, line 623
header: **Source:** [`research-journal.md`](../research-journal.md) — Round 7, line 566; "The ten things that stand" §10, line 623

> What *is* true is the qualitative statement both agents converged on: the words are **finitely supported and eventually identically zero**, hence non-recurrent, so they cannot be Sturmian (Morse–Hedlund: p(L) = L+1 for all L ⟺ Sturmian ⟺ a coding of an irrational rotation), and p(L) **saturates** rather than growing linearly. So the complexity law is OPEN and the Sturmian reading is dead.
Restated among the ten things that stand:

> The greedy word itself is finitely supported, eventually zero, non-recurrent, hence **not Sturmian** (Morse–Hedlund) and **not a rotation sequence** — three-distance belongs to the constant-threshold model the handoff replaced.

header: **Status:** CITED (literature — Fibonacci–Sylvester, Curtiss 1922; verified exhaustively for q ≤ 30)

**Source:** [`research-journal.md`](../research-journal.md) — "Status of the starting claims", line 19; Round 1 (b), line 131; Round 1 status table, lines 152–153; Round 1 Agent B audit, line 167; Round 10 table, line 679
> Rational θ/π ⇒ greedy Egyptian fraction, terminates; θ=π selects {0,1,4} since ½+⅓+⅙=1.

> Exhaustive exact-rational rerun over all reduced p/q with q ≤ 30: **268 of 277 terminate**, and the nine that had not terminated within 200 000 terms (4/17, 14/19, 17/19, 7/23, 21/23, 4/25, 9/29, 12/29, 27/29) are slow, not divergent — this is Curtiss's 1922 theorem (greedy/Sylvester expansion of a rational terminates). Hardest concrete case measured: 19/23 terminates in 5 terms, last index **138458**. Unit fractions 1/k terminate in exactly one term at index k−2.

documents.title: Theorem (the altitude of RH)
documents.source_line: ** [`rh5.html`](../rh5.html) — §4 "ZFC on the circles, and the altitude of RH", theorem box at lines 582–585
header: **Source:** [`rh5.html`](../rh5.html) — §4 "ZFC on the circles, and the altitude of RH", theorem box at lines 582–585

> RH is a Π⁰₁ statement of arithmetic: a single universal quantifier over a decidable matrix. Two certificates. **Analytic:** RH ⟺ |ψ(x) − x| ≤ √x log²x / 8π for all x ≥ 73.2 (Schoenfeld's effective von Koch) — each instance a finite computation over the gears. **Purely gear-side:** RH ⟺ σ(n) < eγ n log log n for every n > 5040 (Robin), with Lagarias's unconditional dressing σ(n) ≤ Hn + eHn log Hn for all n ≥ 1.
- Π⁰₁: a single universal quantifier over a decidable matrix; arithmetic statements are absolute between a universe of sets and its forcing extensions (Shoenfield).
